title: WebMapX Layer Repository — Availability Record
description: Machine-written uptime history. Two shapes share it: one per provider file at status/<same path as the provider file>, keyed by layer id and written by scripts/test-layers.mjs; and one per source at status/sources/<source-id>.json, keyed by source id and written by scripts/check-sources.mjs. Availability is a property of an endpoint, so a harvested service is probed once rather than through every layer it yields. Kept out of the provider files so curated data stays hand-editable and its diffs stay readable. Never edit by hand.

provider.description: provider.id of the file this records

source.description: Path of the provider file, relative to layers/, e.g. 'world/esri.json'

url.description: Endpoint probed, for a source record: the URL harvesting itself reads.

endpoints.description: Source records: history keyed by source id. Same record shape as `layers`.

summary.description: Derived from checks on every write, so the UI can rank without recomputing. Regenerable — checks is the source of truth.

uptime.description: up / probes that reached a verdict. Probes recorded as unknown are excluded from both — a layer we could not test is not a layer that failed. null when no probe has yet reached a verdict: no evidence, which is not the same as 0%.

untested.description: Probes recorded as unknown, e.g. a missing API key. A high count means the uptime figure rests on little evidence.

consecutiveFailures.description: Failing probes since the last up. Drives the 'looks abandoned' signal.

checks.description: Oldest first, appended one per run. Capped at 104 entries — two years of the weekly cron — by dropping from the front; summary.firstChecked keeps the start date after entries roll off.

httpStatus.description: Absent when no HTTP response was received

ms.description: Round-trip time. A service degrading before it fails shows up here first.

reason.description: Error text, for unreachable or unknown

layersOffered.description: How many layers the endpoint offered at probe time. A changed count means the service admin added, renamed or withdrew layers and the harvest is stale.
